# dlaqz1

> Sets `v` to a scalar multiple of the first column of the QZ shift product.

<section class="intro">

for a 3-by-3 matrix pencil `(A,B)`.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlaqz1 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlaqz1';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlaqz1( order, A, LDA, B, LDB, sr1, sr2, si, beta1, beta2, v, strideV ) → Float64Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × N</sub> | The 3-by-3 matrix `A` |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A` (must be `>= 3`) |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × N</sub> | The 3-by-3 matrix `B` |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `B` (must be `>= 3`) |
| `sr1` | `number` | Real part of the first shift |
| `sr2` | `number` | Real part of the second shift |
| `si` | `number` | Imaginary part of the shift |
| `beta1` | `number` | First beta scalar |
| `beta2` | `number` | Second beta scalar |
| `v` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output array of length `>= 3` |
| ↳ `strideV` | `integer` | Stride length for `v` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `A`: The 3-by-3 matrix A in (\*).
- `B`: The 3-by-3 matrix B in (\*).
- `v`: A scalar multiple of the first column of the matrix K in (\*).

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `v`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlaqz1.strided(
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    sr1, sr2, si, beta1, beta2,
    v, strideV, offsetV
) → Float64Array
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × N</sub> | The 3-by-3 matrix `A` |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × N</sub> | The 3-by-3 matrix `B` |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `B` |
| `sr1` | `number` | Real part of the first shift |
| `sr2` | `number` | Real part of the second shift |
| `si` | `number` | Imaginary part of the shift |
| `beta1` | `number` | First beta scalar |
| `beta2` | `number` | Second beta scalar |
| `v` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output array of length `>= 3` |
| ↳ `strideV` | `integer` | Stride length for `v` |
| ↳ `offsetV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `v` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `A`: The 3-by-3 matrix A in (\*).
- `B`: The 3-by-3 matrix B in (\*).
- `v`: A scalar multiple of the first column of the matrix K in (\*).

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `v`

</section>

-   `dlaqz1()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLAQZ1`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlaqz1.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlaqz1 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlaqz1';

// Column-major 3x3 matrices A and B:
const A = new Float64Array( [ 4.0, 2.0, 0.0, 1.0, 5.0, 3.0, 0.5, 1.0, 6.0 ] );
const B = new Float64Array( [ 2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.5, 3.0, 0.0, 0.1, 0.5, 4.0 ] );
let v = new Float64Array( 3 );

// Standard interface:
dlaqz1( 'column-major', A, 3, B, 3, 1.0, 2.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, v, 1 );
console.log( v );

// strided interface:
v = new Float64Array( 3 );
dlaqz1.strided( A, 1, 3, 0, B, 1, 3, 0, 1.0, 2.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, v, 1, 0 );
console.log( v );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLAQZ1`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

Given a 3-by-3 matrix pencil (A,B), DLAQZ1 sets v to a scalar multiple of the first column of the product

(\*) K = (A - (beta2\*sr2 - $i \, \mathrm{si}$)\*B)\*B^(-1)\*(beta1\*A - (sr2 + i\*si2)\*B)\*B^(-1).

It is assumed that either

1) sr1 = sr2 or 2) $\mathrm{si} = 0$.

This is useful for starting double implicit shift bulges in the QZ algorithm.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
